newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba silent on reported bomb incidents.
newsitem.headline: Cuba silent on reported bomb incidents.

text.p: Cuba on Monday declined comment on a U.S. newspaper report that at least one bomb exploded and two others were deactivated at tourist hotels on the communist-ruled island several weeks ago.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Miguel Alfonso told Reuters the ministry had no comment on the report in Saturday's Miami Herald. The ministry has declined comment for several weeks on questions from foreign reporters about persistent rumours in Havana that a small bomb exploded, causing no injuries, and at least one other explosive device was found and deactivated in one or more hotels during April and early May.

Diplomatic sources in Havana say they believe a small bomb exploded during the night in mid-April in the Ache discotheque of the five-star Melia Cohiba hotel in Havana, causing damage but no injuries. Officials at the Sol Melia hotel chain in Spain that runs the Melia Cohiba have said the explosion was caused by a faulty gas pipe.
The discotheque, on the ground floor of the high-rise hotel, was closed after the explosion for an overhaul. It is shortly to reopen as a cafe.

The Miami Herald said another bomb was found and deactivated the same day on an upper floor of the Melia Cohiba. The newspaper said another bomb was deactivated at a hotel in the tourist resort of Varadero, east of Havana.

Whether or not the reported incidents were confirmed, the Cuban government would be concerned to preserve the island's image as a safe and orderly place to visit. Violent crime involving firearms or explosives is very rare in Cuba.
